title: Quiche with meat, poultry or fish

content.title: About
content.content: Quiche with meat, poultry or fish is an open pastry filled with an egg‑cream mixture and a chosen protein (beef, chicken, turkey, fish). The crust can be shortcrust, puff pastry or yeasted dough, and the filling is often enriched with vegetables, cheese and herbs. The dish is a staple of European cuisine and can be served hot or cold.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Quiche originated in medieval France and originally contained no eggs, only milk and cheese.
There are more than 30 regional quiche variations in France, each with its own set of fillings.
Traditional French quiche is often cut into triangular slices for serving.
Quiche can be baked in a conventional oven or microwaved, but only the oven creates a golden crust.
In the United States the classic “Quiche Lorraine” uses bacon and cheese without meat, poultry or fish.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Meat, poultry or fish provide high‑quality protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: Eggs and meat contain vitamin B12, niacin and riboflavin, supporting energy metabolism.

items.title: Contains iron
items.content: Red meat and liver, often used in quiche, are good sources of easily absorbed iron.

items.title: Calcium from cream and cheese
items.content: The dairy components contribute calcium for strong bones and teeth.

items.title: Beneficial fats
items.content: Fish, especially fatty varieties, adds omega‑3 fatty acids that support heart and brain health.

items.title: High calorie content
items.content: Quiche contains cream, cheese and pastry, so portions should be moderate for weight management.

items.title: Saturated fat
items.content: Dairy and meat can raise cholesterol levels if consumed excessively.

items.title: Food‑borne infection risk
items.content: Undercooked chicken, turkey or fish may harbor salmonella or listeria.

items.title: Allergy to eggs or dairy
items.content: People with egg or milk allergies should use alternative recipes.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Quiche is served warm, slightly cooled, or completely cold. Cut into serving slices and pair with a green salad, fresh vegetables or a light vinaigrette. Mustard or tartar sauce can be added for extra flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Cool the baked quiche to room temperature, then cover with plastic wrap and refrigerate for up to 3 days. For longer storage, freeze in an airtight container – it keeps well for up to 2 months. Before reheating, ensure the interior reaches at least 75 °C.
